{{respell|GOR-ghee JENG}}; born January 18, 1990){{cite web|title=2011–12 Louisville Cardinals media guide|url=http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/lou/sports/m-baskbl/auto_pdf/2011-12/misc_non_event/mbb-1112-mg-section-3.pdf|access-date=May 19, 2012|work=CSTV.com|archive-date=March 4, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304121122/http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/lou/sports/m-baskbl/auto_pdf/2011-12/misc_non_event/mbb-1112-mg-section-3.pdf|url-status=dead}} is a Senegalese former professional [[basketball]] player currently working as a basketball operations representative with the [[San Antonio Spurs]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played college basketball for the [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville Cardinals]]. Dieng was selected as the 21st overall pick in the [[2013 NBA draft]] by the [[Utah Jazz]] and was traded on draft night to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]]. He spent seven seasons with the team before being dealt to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in February 2020. He reached a contract buyout agreement with the Grizzlies in March 2021 and joined the [[San Antonio Spurs]] in free agency. He signed with the Hawks in August 2021. In July 2022, he returned to the Spurs. On December 9, 2023, Dieng retired from basketball. ==High school career== Dieng attended the Sports for Education and Economic Development (SEEDS) Academy in [[Thiès]], [[Senegal]].{{cite web|title=Alumni- SEEDS|url=http://www.seedproject.org/seeds-academy/alumni|access-date=May 19, 2012|work=SEEDProjecy.org|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131102173226/http://www.seedproject.org/seeds-academy/alumni|archive-date=November 2, 2013}} While at SEEDS, Dieng had a 3.2 [[GPA]]. Dieng played in the national [[Nationale 1 (Senegal)|Nationale 1]] league with [[US Rail]], and helped the team win the [[Senegalese Basketball Cup|Senegalese Cup]] in 2009, scoring 19 points in the final and being named final MVP.{{Cite web |date=2024-06-11 |title=Basket : la coupe du Sénégal emprunte les Rails |url=https://www.au-senegal.com/Basket-la-coupe-du-Senegal.html |access-date=2024-06-11 |website=Au Sénégal, le cœur du Sénégal |language=fr}} He was invited to the [[Basketball Without Borders]] camp in [[South Africa]] in 2009 as one of 60 promising players selected from across Africa, and was named [[Most valuable player|MVP]] of the camp.[http://bwb.fiba.com/camps/2009/johannesburg "BWB Africa 2009."] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150518091818/http://bwb.fiba.com/camps/2009/johannesburg |date=May 18, 2015 }}, ''[[FIBA]]''. Retrieved on May 4, 2015.{{cite news|title=NCAA Tournament in Phoenix: 'Throwback' Gorgui Dieng hits potential at a perfect time for Louisville|url=http://www.azcentral.com/sports/colleges/articles/2012/03/23/20120323ncaa-tournament-phoenix-throwback-gorgui-dieng-louisville.html|work=AZCentral.com|access-date=March 22, 2012|date=March 22, 2012}} Dieng transferred to [[Huntington Prep School|Huntington Prep]] in [[West Virginia]] for the 2009–10 school year, where he played for coach Rob Fulford. He averaged 15.4 points, 12.6 rebounds and 7.2 blocks per game during his senior season at Huntington Prep.{{cite web|title=Gorgui Dieng Profile|url=http://www.uoflsports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/dieng_gorgui00.html|work=University of Louisville athletics|access-date=May 19, 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120616182020/http://www.uoflsports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/dieng_gorgui00.html|archive-date=June 16, 2012}} ===Recruiting=== Dieng was recruited by [[Marquette University|Marquette]], [[Marshall University|Marshall]], [[University of Colorado|Colorado]], and [[University of Louisville|Louisville]] among others who came in late. His high school coach Rob Fulford said "Academics are no question, He passed the SAT six months after learning English and passed with 400 points to spare."{{cite web|last=Taylor |first=Grant |title=Huntington Prep's Dieng commits to Louisville |url=http://www.herald-dispatch.com/sports/x874716903/Preps-Dieng-commits-to-Louisville |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130125102510/http://www.herald-dispatch.com/sports/x874716903/Preps-Dieng-commits-to-Louisville |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 25, 2013 |work=herald-dispatch.com |date=April 27, 2010 |access-date=May 19, 2012 }} The most interest was from Louisville and Marshall. Then on March 30, 2010, head coach [[Donnie Jones (basketball)|Donnie Jones]] left Marshall to become the head coach of the [[University of Central Florida]]. The next day, [[Rick Pitino]] signed a contract extension through 2017 with Louisville. On April 26, 2010, Dieng verbally committed to Louisville. Louisville assistant coach [[Walter McCarty]], who has NBA experience, helped Rick Pitino land Dieng in a Cardinals uniform. Considered a four-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Dieng was listed as the No. 10 power forward and the No. 44 player in the nation in 2010.{{cite news|title=Gorgui Dieng Recruiting Profile|url=https://rivals.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Gorgui-Dieng-106796;_ylt=AneHOJbxDJea5HNu3bj.b5DXO5B4|work=Rivals.com|access-date=October 5, 2010}} ==College career== [[File:Gorgui Dieng 2013.jpg|thumb|left|Dieng in 2013 with Louisville|260x260px]] Dieng was ruled ineligible by the NCAA when he first arrived at Louisville forcing them to hold him out of practice and individual workouts.{{cite news|title=Louisville freshman Gorgui Dieng ruled ineligible|url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/college/mensbasketball/bigeast/2010-10-05-louisville-dieng-ineligible_N.htm|work=usatoday.com | date=October 5, 2010 |access-date=October 5, 2010}} Louisville appealed the NCAA's decision and on October 26, 2010, it was announced that the NCAA reversed its original decision and ruled Dieng eligible immediately.{{cite web|last=Brown|first=C.L.|title=Louisville's Gorgui Dieng ruled eligible by NCAA after appeal|url=http://www.courier-journal.com/article/20101026/SPORTS02/310260064/Louisville-s-Gorgui-Dieng-ruled-eligible-by-NCAA-after-appeal|work=courier-journal.com|date=October 26, 2010|access-date=October 26, 2010}} As a freshman Dieng saw action in 29 games averaging 16 mins a game. He scored 5.7 points a game, pulled down 4.4 rebounds and blocked 1.9 shots a game in his limited action.{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/gorgui-dieng-1.html |title=Gorgui Dieng Stats | College Basketball at |publisher=Sports-reference.com |access-date=April 9, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130421011241/http://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/gorgui-dieng-1.html |archive-date=April 21, 2013 }} The Cardinals finished the 2010–11 season with a 25–10 record, 12–6 in Big East play tied for 3rd and lost in the championship game of the [[2011 Big East men's basketball tournament]] to Connecticut. They received an at-large bid and a #4 seed in the 2011 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament where they were upset in the first round by #13 seeded [[2010–11 Morehead State Eagles men's basketball team|Morehead State]].{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/schools/louisville/2011-schedule.html |title=2010–11 Louisville Cardinals Schedule and Results | College Basketball at |publisher=Sports-reference.com |access-date=April 9, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131105142552/http://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/schools/louisville/2011-schedule.html |archive-date=November 5, 2013 }} As a sophomore, Dieng started at [[center (basketball)|center]] for the [[2011–12 Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team|2011–12 Louisville team]] that reached the Final Four of the [[2012 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|NCAA tournament]]. In the 2011–12 season, Dieng led the [[Big East Conference]] in [[block (basketball)|blocks]], and set the all-time school record for blocks in a season.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=320680269|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210422170508/https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=320680269|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 22, 2021|title=Louisville-Marquette game recap|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=March 9, 2012|access-date=March 9, 2012}} On March 22, 2012, Dieng matched a Louisville tournament record with 7 blocks in a game All-Tournament Team]] (2012) *2nd in all time blocks in [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Cardinal]] history (267 blocks) ==Professional career== ===Minnesota Timberwolves (2013–2020)=== [[File:Dieng-20190120.jpg|thumb|Dieng with the Timberwolves in 2019]] On June 27, 2013, Dieng was selected by the [[Utah Jazz]] with the 21st overall pick in the [[2013 NBA draft]], and then traded to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] along with [[Shabazz Muhammad]] the 14th pick later that night in exchange for the 9th pick [[Trey Burke]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2013/news/06/27/wolves-trade-burke-for-picks.ap/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130701025146/http://www.nba.com/2013/news/06/27/wolves-trade-burke-for-picks.ap|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 1, 2013|title=Report: Wolves trade Burke to Jazz for 2 picks|work=NBA.com|date=June 27, 2013|access-date=October 31, 2016}} On March 20, 2014, in a game against the [[Houston Rockets]], Dieng recorded 22 points and 21 rebounds, the first ever 20–20 game by a rookie in Timberwolves' franchise history. He also became just the sixth player since the NBA began tracking starts in 1970 to have at least 20 points and 20 rebounds within their first three career starts.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20140320/MINHOU/gameinfo.html|title=Harden leads Rockets over Timberwolves 129-106|work=NBA.com|date=March 20, 2014|access-date=March 20, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140331142754/http://www.nba.com/games/20140320/MINHOU/gameinfo.html|archive-date=March 31, 2014|url-status=dead}} On April 11, also against the Rockets, Dieng scored the game-winning basket with 4.6 seconds left and finished with 12 points and 20 rebounds.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20140411/HOUMIN/gameinfo.html|title=Notebook: Wolves 112, Rockets 110|work=NBA.com|date=April 11, 2014|access-date=April 11, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140412020354/http://www.nba.com/games/20140411/HOUMIN/gameinfo.html|archive-date=April 12, 2014|url-status=dead}} As a result of his improvements throughout the second half of the season, Dieng was named to the [[NBA All-Rookie Team|NBA All-Rookie second team]]. On January 12, 2015, Dieng tied his career high of 22 points in a loss to the [[Denver Nuggets]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150105/DENMIN/gameinfo.html|title=Afflalo, Nuggets hand Wolves 12th straight loss|work=NBA.com|date=January 5, 2015|access-date=January 5, 2015}} On January 28, he was named a representative of ''Team World'' to compete in the 2015 [[Rising Stars Challenge]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/dieng-muhammad-lavine-and-wiggins-represent-wolves-2015-bbva-compass-rising-stars-challenge|title=Dieng, LaVine, Muhammad and Wiggins to Represent Wolves in 2015 BBVA Compass Rising Stars Challenge|work=NBA.com|date=January 28, 2015|access-date=January 28, 2015}} On August 1, 2015, Dieng played for Team Africa at the [[NBA Africa Game 2015|2015 NBA Africa exhibition game]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/13359599/nba-current-former-stars-put-show-africa-exhibition|title=NBA stars, legends shine as Team World rallies to beat Team Africa|publisher=ESPN|date=August 1, 2015|access-date=August 1, 2015}} On December 20, 2015, Dieng had a then season-best game with 20 points and 10 rebounds in a 100–85 win over the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151220/MINBKN/gameinfo.html|title=Towns has 24 points, 10 rebounds as Wolves win in Brooklyn|work=NBA.com|date=December 20, 2015|access-date=December 20, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151221023044/http://www.nba.com/games/20151220/MINBKN/gameinfo.html|archive-date=December 21, 2015|url-status=dead}} On February 6, 2016, he recorded a career-high 24 points, 13 rebounds and seven assists in a 112–105 win over the [[Chicago Bulls]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160206/CHIMIN/gameinfo.html|title=Timberwolves close out Bulls with 12-0 run to win 112-105|work=NBA.com|date=February 6, 2016|access-date=February 7, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180303191113/http://www.nba.com/games/20160206/CHIMIN/gameinfo.html|archive-date=March 3, 2018|url-status=dead}} On October 31, 2016, Dieng signed a four-year, $64 million contract extension with the Timberwolves.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/timberwolves-sign-gorgui-dieng-contract-extension|title=TIMBERWOLVES SIGN GORGUI DIENG TO CONTRACT EXTENSION|work=NBA.com|date=October 31, 2016|access-date=October 31, 2016}}{{cite web|last=Charania|first=Shams|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/news/sources-gorgui-dieng-finalizing-64m-extension-with-minnesota-214835037.html|title=Sources: Gorgui Dieng finalizing $64M extension with Minnesota|work=Yahoo.com|date=October 31, 2016|access-date=October 31, 2016}} On January 15, 2017, he scored a season-high 21 points in a 98–87 loss to the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{cite web|url=http://www.foxsports.com/north/story/gorgui-dieng-minnesota-timberwolves-scores-season-high-but-wolves-lose-in-dallas-011517|title=Dieng scores season high, but Wolves lose in Dallas|work=FoxSports.com|date=January 15, 2017|access-date=March 30, 2017}} On March 30, 2017, he recorded 11 points, a season-high 15 rebounds, six assists and three blocks in a 119–104 win over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com.au/nba/recap?gameId=400900518|title=Rubio scores career-high 33 as Wolves beat Lakers 119-104|work=ESPN.com|date=March 30, 2017|access-date=March 30, 2017}} ===Memphis Grizzlies (2020–2021)=== On February 6, 2020, Dieng was acquired by the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in a three-team trade also involving the [[Miami Heat]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-acquire-justise-winslow-gorgui-dieng-and-dion-waiters-in-three-team-trade-with-miami-heat-and-minnesota-timberwolves-200206|title=Memphis Grizzlies acquire Justise Winslow, Gorgui Dieng and Dion Waiters in three-team trade with Miami Heat and Minnesota Timberwolves|work=NBA.com|date=February 6, 2020|access-date=February 6, 2020}} The Grizzlies also acquired [[Justise Winslow]] and [[Dion Waiters]] who was later waived. The Heat acquired [[Andre Iguodala]], [[Solomon Hill (basketball)|Solomon Hill]] and [[Jae Crowder]] while the Timberwolves acquired [[James Johnson (basketball, born 1987)|James Johnson]]. On March 26, 2021, Dieng and the Grizzlies reached a contract buyout agreement.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-waive-gorgui-dieng-210326|title=Memphis Grizzlies waive Gorgui Dieng|work=NBA.com|date=March 26, 2021|access-date=March 26, 2021}} ===San Antonio Spurs (2021)=== On March 29, 2021, Dieng signed with the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{cite web |title=Spurs sign Gorgui Dieng |url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/spurs-sign-gorgui-dieng |website=NBA.com |access-date=March 29, 2021 |date=March 29, 2021}} He averaged 5.3 PPG, 2.6 RPG, and 1.2 APG in 16 games played off the bench with the Spurs.{{cite web|title=Gorgui Dieng stats|url=https://www.nba.com/stats/player/203476/|website=NBA.com|access-date=August 3, 2021|date=August 3, 2021}} ===Atlanta Hawks (2021–2022)=== On August 9, 2021, Dieng signed a 1-year, $4 million contract with the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/atlanta-hawks-sign-gorgui-dieng|title=Atlanta Hawks |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2943704-gorgui-dieng-hawks-reportedly-agree-to-1-year-4m-contract-in-free-agency |access-date=March 7, 2022 |website=Bleacher Report}} ===Return to San Antonio (2022–2023)=== On July 5, 2022, Dieng signed a contract to return to the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{cite web|first=Brett|last=Siegel|title=San Antonio Spurs Sign Veteran Center Gorgui Dieng|url=https://www.si.com/fannation/nba/fastbreak/news/san-antonio-spurs-sign-veteran-center-gorgui-dieng-who-played-for-the-minnesota-timberwolves-memphis-grizzlies-and-atlanta-hawks|website=SI.com|date=July 5, 2022|access-date=July 5, 2022}} On January 5, 2023, he was waived by the Spurs.{{cite web|title=Celtics trade Noah Vonleh, cash to Spurs|url=https://www.nba.com/news/celtics-spurs-trade-noah-vonleh|website=NBA.com|date=January 5, 2023|access-date=January 8, 2023}} Three days later, he signed a 10-day contract with the Spurs.{{cite web|title=Spurs' Gorgui Dieng: Inks 10-day deal|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/spurs-gorgui-dieng-inks-10-day-deal/|website=CBSSports.com|date=January 8, 2023|access-date=January 8, 2023}} On January 20, he signed a second 10-day contract with San Antonio.{{cite web|title=Spurs' Gorgui Dieng: Lands another 10-day contract|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/spurs-gorgui-dieng-lands-another-10-day-contract|website=CBSSports.com|date=January 20, 2023|access-date=January 20, 2023}} On February 10, Dieng re-signed with the Spurs for the remainder of the season.{{cite web|title=SPURS SIGN GORGUI DIENG|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-sign-gorgui-dieng-3|website=NBA.com|date=February 10, 2023|access-date=July 25, 2023}} On December 9, 2023, Dieng revealed in an interview with the ''[[San Antonio Express-News]]'' that he had officially retired from professional basketball.{{Cite web |last=Stinar |first=Ben |date=2023-12-09 |title=10-Year NBA Veteran Is Officially Retired |url=https://www.si.com/fannation/nba/fastbreak/news/10-year-nba-veteran-is-officially-retired-san-antonio-spurs-gorgui-dieng |access-date=2023-12-16 |website=Fastbreak on FanNation |language=en}}
